Yes, I would say that the sensory apparatus and brain are species-specific icons. My entire body is just an icon. 
When I move my hand and grab something, even that movement is just an icon. I don't know what I am really doing in 
objective reality—I only know my own actions under the limits of the descriptions available within my interface. Genes, 
animals, species, and even spacetime itself are just icons. 
The evolutionary arguments against true perceptions do not hold against true logic and math, since we do need 
to reason about fitness payoffs—two bites of an apple give roughly twice the payoff as one bite, for instance. There are 
no selection pressures to be geniuses at math and logic, and few of us are. But we need to have enough competence to 
get the payoffs we need. 
I wouldn't say that the spacetime universe is itself a conscious agent, but that it is the format of the interface of 
human conscious agents. 
I am working on a mathematical theory of how conscious agents evolve languages to better understand each 
other. It seems that they can get more information about each other without violating the second law of 
thermodynamics, if they hillclimb mutual information. Fun research ahead on this one! 
Love, 
Don
